adjudicated.jp: 去年の初夏だった。
adjudicated.en: It was last year, early Summer,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 新川豊と出会ったのは。
adjudicated.en: when I had my meeting with Shinkawa Yutaka.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 蝉のうるさい夏だった。
adjudicated.en: It was a Summer of loud cicadas.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 偶然、ぶつかった。
adjudicated.en: We bumped into each other, a coincidence.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 妙に会話が弾んで。
adjudicated.en: An odd conversation was stimulated.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that their conversation became strangely lively. The English makes the conversation itself odd and treats it as something externally stimulated.

adjudicated.jp: ウマがあった。
adjudicated.en: We got along well, as if a rider and his horse.
comments: Expanded hyperliteral, given their relationship wasn't that far off. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ウマが合う is an idiom meaning that they hit it off. The English translates that meaning and then redundantly exposes the source idiom as a new literal comparison.

highlights.text: as if a rider and his horse

adjudicated.jp: 群青には完全に自分の世界で生きている者もいる。
adjudicated.en:
In Gunjou, there are people who live entirely
into their world,
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says some people at Gunjō live entirely in worlds of their own. The English uses non-Hepburn 'Gunjou' and the wrong preposition 'into.'

adjudicated.jp: 人を傷つけやすい者もいる。
adjudicated.en: as well as people who easily hurt others.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ある頃から、世界は狂人を生み出しはじめた。
adjudicated.en:
Ever since a time, the world had begun to give
birth to madmen.
adjudicated.assessment: ある頃から means 'from a certain point' or 'at some point.' The English phrase is not idiomatic and past perfect lacks a later past anchor.

highlights.text: Ever since a time, the world had begun

adjudicated.jp: その多くが人を傷つけた。
adjudicated.en: Many of them injured people.
adjudicated.assessment: 人を傷つけた includes psychological and interpersonal harm in this discussion. 'Injured' narrows it to physical injury.

adjudicated.jp: 心の病は、ただ己だけの問題ではなくなっていた。
adjudicated.en:
The illness of the heart was no longer merely
a personal problem.
adjudicated.assessment: 心の病 here means mental illness, not a cardiac disease or a metaphorical illness of the heart.

adjudicated.jp: 原因はわからない。
adjudicated.en: Origin is unknown.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the cause is unknown. The English chooses a different noun and omits the required article.

adjudicated.jp: 政府はいくつかの対策を打ち出したが、その内容が広く報道されることはなかった。
adjudicated.en:
The government had worked out a number of
countermeasures, but the specifics of those
were not widely reported on.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 水面下で動いている、と曜子ちゃんは言っていた。
adjudicated.en:
Motion beneath the water surface, said
Youko-chan. All behind closed doors.
comments: Keeping literal water surface, see CCC3012A. It's only maybe a very odd thing for Youko to say since she likely knows of this thing of his - may be why she immediately assumes an observer of worlds in CCD0021. While "beneath the water surface" would be all Youko says, because Youko, it's not clear enough in English so specified. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Youko says that measures are moving below the surface. The English produces a subjectless fragment from the literal water image and then adds the separate idiom 'behind closed doors.'

highlights.text:
Motion beneath the water surface, said
Youko-chan. All behind closed doors.

adjudicated.jp: 詳細は不明。
adjudicated.en: Details are unclear.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 少なくとも、世界が緩慢な狂気に浸されていることは……自分の胸に聞けばよく理解できた。
adjudicated.en:
At the very least, the world was sinking into
a slow insanity... and if I listened to my
heart I could very well understand.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: だから群青学院は存在した。
adjudicated.en: That is why Gunjou Institute existed.
adjudicated.assessment: The place name 群青 is romanized Gunjō in standard Hepburn. 'Gunjou' uses an ad hoc ou sequence without recorded official Latin-script evidence.

adjudicated.jp: 隔離施設として。
adjudicated.en: As an isolation facility.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 留年は日常茶飯事。
adjudicated.en: Repeating class years is an ordinary event.
comments: So it'd be technically impossible to figure out which year anyone actually is, how old anyone is based on class, or what year it even is. And they say Cross Channel doesn't explain stuff. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: だが何年かけても症状が回復しない者は、さらなる施設へと送られる。
adjudicated.en:
Yet, the people whose conditions do not recover
after some years are sent to a further facility.
comments: Maybe that Research Building of CCA0022, maybe just Class X. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そういう人々は、ほとんど他者との接触を必要としない。
adjudicated.en:
People like those require almost no contact
with others.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 独力で生きる力には欠けているが、当人の心は、もう人のそれを離れてしまっているのだ。
adjudicated.en:
Their power to live by their strength is lacking,
but their hearts are already distanced from
those of others.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says they lack the ability to live independently and that their minds have departed from the human kind. 'Live by their strength' misstates independence, while 'distanced from those of others' weakens the categorical second clause.

highlights.text:
Their power to live by their strength is lacking,
but their hearts are already distanced from
those of others.

adjudicated.jp: だから。
adjudicated.en: Therefore,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 群青では友達を作るのは、少し難しい。
adjudicated.en: making friends in Gunjou is somewhat difficult.
adjudicated.assessment: The place name 群青 is Gunjō in standard Hepburn; the English uses the non-Hepburn spelling 'Gunjou.'

adjudicated.jp: 対話が成立しにくいからだ。
adjudicated.en:
Because it is difficult for dialogue to come
into existence.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that successful dialogue or communication is difficult. The English literalizes 成立 as a conversation coming into existence.

highlights.text:
for dialogue to come
into existence

adjudicated.jp: １クラスで、１０人くらいだろうか。
adjudicated.en: In one class, there are about ten people, maybe,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: まともに会話が成り立つのは。
adjudicated.en: that can construct a normal conversation at all.
adjudicated.assessment: 会話が成り立つ means being able to hold or sustain a coherent conversation, not constructing one as an object.

adjudicated.jp: 『ＯＫ、なんとかやっていけそうな気がしてきた』
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: 『Okieh, I got the feeling I can work with this somehow.』
adjudicated.assessment: The source begins with the English loan 'OK.' The invented eye-dialect spelling adds a voice not encoded by that form.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 誰が悪かったのかな。
adjudicated.en: Whose fault was it, I wonder?
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺か。
adjudicated.en: Mine?
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: それともヤツか。
adjudicated.en: Or was it his?
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 結論は出ない。
adjudicated.en: Final words don't come.
adjudicated.assessment: 結論は出ない means that no conclusion presents itself. 'Final words' instead suggests a dying statement or the end of a speech.

adjudicated.jp: 涙も出ない。
adjudicated.en: Tears don't come.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: まだ、出ない。
adjudicated.en: They... still don't come.
comments: Despite having cried plenty of times, there's this subtext about Taichi being unable to cry. I suspect he can't cry about Yutaka, not in general. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
